result.rationale: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema (addGuests.schema.ts) is z.object({bookingId, guests: z.array(z.string().email())}) with no uniqueness check, and the handler's uniqueGuests filter only removes guests matching pre-existing booking.attendees (case-sensitively via `guest === attendee.email`) or the blacklist — it never deduplicates guests within the same request. The uniqueness refine exists only in the client dialog's local ZAddGuestsInputSchema. So a direct API call with duplicated emails creates duplicate Attendee rows via createMany. Mechanism fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts duplicate emails and addGuests.handler's filter only removes guests matching pre-existing attendees (case-sensitively), so one request containing the same email twice creates two Attendee rows for the booking — uniqueness is enforced only in the client dialog's local zod refine, never at the API boundary. A direct tRPC call with guests ['a@b.com','a@b.com'] (or 'A@B.com' plus 'a@b.com') persists duplicate attendee records for the same bookingId, and the duplicated address appears twice in evt.attendees and the ICS attendee list, receiving duplicate emails.
